title: 104 Satellites on One Rocket

segments.say: One rocket. A hundred and four satellites. In February twenty seventeen, ISRO set a world record.
On the fifteenth of February, twenty seventeen, the PSLV-C37 lifted off from Sriharikota. Within about half an hour, all one hundred and four satellites were in orbit.
Only three were Indian. A hundred and one belonged to six other countries, most of them small nano-satellites from the United States.

anim.title: How not to crash them
items: Set apart in time and direction

segments.say: The hard part was letting them go without collisions. They were released one by one, in a careful order, at slightly different angles.
The PSLV, seen here on a later flight, had already earned a name as ISRO's reliable workhorse. This launch also showed India could sell space rides.

anim.title: Why it mattered
items: A world record at the time

segments.say: The record stood for nearly four years. More importantly, it put India on the map of commercial launches.
For GS Three: PSLV-C37, a hundred and four satellites, and the main passenger, a Cartosat-2 series Earth-observation satellite.

sources: ISRO, PSLV-C37 mission page and press release, 15 February 2017: 104 satellites launched in a single flight; Cartosat-2 series satellite was the primary payload; two Indian nano-satellites; 101 international customer satellites from six countries (USA, Netherlands, Switzerland, Israel, Kazakhstan, UAE)
PIB, 15 February 2017: world record for the number of satellites launched in a single mission
SpaceX Transporter-1 (24 January 2021) launched 143 satellites, surpassing the record

quiz.q: How many satellites did PSLV-C37 launch?
How many of them were foreign?

quiz.why: The primary passenger was a Cartosat-2 series Earth-observation satellite.

reviewNote: Facts were read against ISRO's PSLV-C37 page and the PIB release. The only photo is of a later PSLV flight and is described as such. Moving facts: the record was broken in 2021, said as 'stood for nearly four years'.
